title: Integrate Prism crystal artwork and two-zone wall animation
body:
## Desired outcome

Replace the wall's current artwork with the approved Prism crystal finish and a layout-driven mechanical assembly. The moving UI must use the same detailed components as the finished artwork, with bright cores and diffuse light spilling beyond the crystal.

## Scope and accepted decisions

Integrate the existing Prism finish kit into the current browser wall map. The separately planned Linux installation retains that UI, so reuse the existing application operations and make the assets portable with the wall server. No Windows tray artwork, tray animation, Windows Forms, service migration, or installation work is included.

The source reference is the owner-provided `prism-finish-kit.zip`, verified during planning with SHA-256 `ceef5c07993fa3aba77daae02521747fbb55d1c8595002231a378d06105f8fb0`. Its `INTEGRATION.md`, `prism.js`, `adapters.js`, component assets, layout fixtures, and exports are the implementation handoff. Round nine is the clean-start motion reference; the finish kit supplies the polished material. Import the selected reusable sources and reproducible asset build through this delivery's PR. Do not depend at runtime on a personal artifact directory. Confirm the matching archive is available before asset work; an unavailable archive blocks visual acceptance, not permission to invent replacements.

The approved UI rhythm is two seconds. Physical light behavior and timing remain unchanged. The kit's 2.6-second cycle, global light mode, single-selection model, disabled interaction during assembly, and controller-first root choice require adaptation to existing app behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] AC1: Render thicker faceted crystal tubes with a bold, bright core, long visible tail, and broad diffuse spill near the approved finish kit's upper glow range. Preserve crisp bevels and a hexagonal central connector. Tubes meet the flat faces of connectors. Static and animated poses use the same scalable material components and app-resolved colors; no screenshot replacement or fixed demo shape.
- [x] AC2: Each connector and Line can animate independently around its connection. From the existing most-connected hub selection, all hub-connected Lines begin together; tubes eject at full thickness and rotate with their connector into position, then assembly proceeds outward. The hub rotates with its attached structure. Other connectors grow from the arriving Line tip and unfold their six permanent inner-border sections clockwise or counterclockwise. No temporary triangle-to-border swap, thin white completion flash, lingering center shutter, or translucent overlay remains. Preserve the existing approximately two-second assembly, independent disconnected components, and exact final positions, including cycle-closing Lines.
- [x] AC3: Each Line retains two independently colored zones with stable endpoint ownership. During Work, every Line carrying a working, question, blocked, or unread task sends two bright packets from its connectors inward in one direction, meeting in a brief center spark within a two-second cycle. Idle Lines stay steady. Quiet is steady with reduced glow; Free is dim/desaturated with the released-state readout. Reduced motion skips assembly and suppresses travel and sparks while keeping modes distinguishable. Preserve red/yellow alerts, project signatures, half swaps, and completion semantics.
- [x] AC4: On first assembly completion, explicit Replay completion, or immediate completion caused by interaction, the UI flow begins at phase zero at both connectors after the structure is in place, when Work/task state permits flow. All active Lines share that phase. Polls, palette changes, selection, mode changes, focus, and reconnects do not randomly offset Lines, replay assembly, or reset the established UI clock. Preserve the page-wide phase across render rebuilds within the existing 50 ms boundary. Keep UI assembly/flow clocks separate from physical task pulse/comet epochs.
- [x] AC5: Preserve opening and map-entry preferences as separate browser-local toggles, existing defaults, and manual Replay. Interaction during assembly completes it immediately and then performs the intended action. Repeated Replay never queues. Geometry changes or connection failures end assembly immediately; the wall settles into the latest polled state with task lists, alerts, and connection information visible. Visibility pause/resume retains the current animation position.
- [x] AC6: Preserve stable Line numbering and IDs, Ctrl/Cmd/Shift multi-selection, keyboard focus, task/project/inspector associations, selection and pending rings, and existing mode controls. Selection, highlighting, animation, and Replay issue no write or Locate request. They do not mark tasks read, change assignments/scenes, mutate reservations, or restart completed effects. `settings.style` remains the existing Classic/Project allocation choice. Luminous-number visibility and collision changes belong to #26; retain current identification until that refinement lands.
- [x] AC7: Use the prerequisite geometry response to draw the saved 15-Line arrangement plus chain, branch, cycle, disconnected, and rotated/flipped fixtures. Malformed or unsupported geometry leaves a usable documented fallback and preserves the last valid layout. Surviving IDs retain selection and current colors through valid geometry replacement. Do not silently claim support for Light Panels, 90-degree connectors, or a 300-Line performance envelope.
- [x] AC8: Serve or build the selected local components through bounded asset paths with correct MIME types. Preserve Host/origin protections and the existing CSP; no arbitrary file server, remote asset dependency, or credential exposure. Verify the packaged wall can run through a foreground Linux server without Windows helpers. Coordinate the asset inclusion list with the Linux installation owner when that work is published, without taking ownership of service setup.
- [x] AC9: Dispose listeners, observers, and animation frames when a renderer is replaced or removed. Hidden hosts/documents pause motion; Quiet, Free, and reduced-motion steady states do not keep an unnecessary animation loop. Repeated state updates and view mounts do not multiply renderers or timers. Capture desktop/mobile and high-DPI visual evidence and frame measurements for the actual 15-Line layout and a documented larger synthetic fixture. Human approval of this implementation's current candidate establishes the final material/motion quality.

## Verification approach

All checks below are planned, not executed by issue publication. The kit's recorded preview checks are reference evidence, not app acceptance.

| Criteria | Planned evidence |
| --- | --- |
| AC1, AC2 | Deterministic assembly poses and high-DPI screenshots compared with the finish kit; assertions for connector-face contact, tip-grown connectors, permanent rim sections, and removed overlays; human visual review of the moving candidate. |
| AC3, AC4 | Controlled-clock browser checks at readiness, inward travel, center collision, fade, and the next cycle; two distinct zone colors and half swaps; active/idle status and mode matrix; phase preserved through updates. |
| AC5, AC6 | Existing assembly and interaction journeys, keyboard/multi-selection tests, replay/cancellation/latest-state cases, and request spies asserting no new writes. Snapshot application epochs and assignments with fake lights. |
| AC7 | API-to-renderer fixture checks across the real arrangement and synthetic topologies, transforms, missing geometry, and valid replacement. |
| AC8 | Foreground Linux packaged-server smoke test, asset MIME/allowlist checks, missing assets and traversal rejection, privacy canaries, and existing security checks. |
| AC9 | Repeated mount/update/dispose checks, hidden/visible and reduced-motion checks, recorded browser frame measurements with the tested fixture/browser identified, and screenshots at 1440, 800, and 390 px. Do not infer installed or physical acceptance from these results. |

## Outcome

Run the Nanoleaf worker, SQLite database, wall map, controller API, and MCP host in Ubuntu WSL on the existing PC. Reuse the separate processes and existing single light writer. Support Codex Desktop tasks executing in WSL and WSL CLI sessions.

Accept device configuration privately and create runtime state under `~/.local/share/codex-nanoleaf` with owner-only permissions. - [x] A2. Reuse the existing hook, CLI, wall-map, controller, and worker processes. All state coordination happens within Linux. Concurrent requests retain the existing worker lock and produce only one light writer.
- [x] A3. Register Linux hook commands while preserving unrelated hooks. Support WSL task execution and the existing configurable Desktop project, title, and unread JSON readers.
- [x] A4. Provide configurable loopback ports, defaulting to wall map `8765`, controller `41231`, and MCP `41230`. Add a command that prints the map URL without launching a browser. Port conflicts return useful errors.
- [x] A5. Configure MCP to use the existing direct HTTP controller transport. Preserve authentication, request identities, revision checks, and Work/Quiet/Free behavior. Linux runtime commands never launch Windows executables.
- [x] A6. Supply user systemd units for the wall map, controller, and MCP host, plus foreground commands. Keep the worker on demand. Document that availability follows WSL's lifetime.
- [x] A7. Update installation instructions, applicable ownership contracts, and issue-linked OpenSpec artifacts with a design and ownership ADR. Link the Hub documentation companion PR and state whether guide synchronization is complete or pending.

## Verification

The table below defines the required checks. Completed source evidence is recorded in the closing receipt and PR #57; installed and physical evidence remains #55.

- Windows and Linux workers must never control the device at the same time. Step 1 comes before step 3.

title: Expose native power, brightness and saved-scene controls through the protected controller API
body:
## Outcome

Advertise and execute power, brightness and saved-scene activation as supported controller v1 capabilities on the protected controller API, so the shared BUNNY frontend can offer Nanoleaf general controls without an agent session.

## Scope and accepted definition

The accepted general-control definition is [Hub #31](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/31), recorded in the hub as ADR 0005 (`docs/decisions/0005-general-device-controls.md`). Released controller v1 already carries `power.set`, `brightness.set` and `scene.activate` in its closed command union, so no shared contract release is needed. The installation's single worker remains the only light writer. Work, Quiet and Free keep their native meanings; there is no global mode.

## Accepted behavior

- Power and brightness are mode-independent: the controller accepts them in Work, Quiet and Free.
- A brightness command is a user override. It persists until the next explicit mode command, which reapplies that mode's brightness policy. This issue owns the exact policy text, including how Work and Quiet effects render while brightness is overridden.
- The controller discovers the device's saved scene identities and advertises them through the `scenes` capability, bounded to 256 IDs. If scene display names are exposed, they travel through the `nanoleaf.integration` extension as user-chosen names from the Nanoleaf app. Nothing else is copied into labels.
- Scene activation is accepted only in Free. In Work or Quiet the command returns a typed v1 failure before any device write, reusing an existing failure code; no new wire value is introduced.
- Scene activation in Free is a one-shot worker write. It starts no polling, and Free continues to perform no controller polling after handoff. Task and effect epochs are preserved.
- Desired power and brightness become known after acceptance. Observed values stay unknown unless the worker holds evidence. Missing evidence is never fabricated.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1.** The capability declaration marks `power`, `brightness` and `scenes` supported with typed constraints while `media`, `zones` and `preview` stay unsupported. All 220 shared fixture cases still pass. A linked Hub companion PR updates the hub's pinned Nanoleaf fixtures and compatibility record.
- [ ] **AC2.** `power.set` and `brightness.set` execute through the existing worker queue with the replay, revision, generation, uncertain-hold and single-writer rules delivered by #28.
- [ ] **AC3.** The brightness override policy above is specified and tested across Work, Quiet and Free transitions, including an override followed by a same-mode command.
- [ ] **AC4.** `scene.activate` uses discovered scene IDs, is accepted only in Free, returns a typed failure otherwise, performs one write with no follow-up polling and preserves epochs.
- [ ] **AC5.** Snapshots keep desired, pending, last successful send, last outcome and observation separate; unknown observation remains unknown.
- [ ] **AC6.** The legacy Windows bridge, tray, wall editor and hooks are unaffected; the full regression and browser suites pass. The exact issue-linked OpenSpec change named after this issue records the protected-controller-api delta.

Physical acceptance on the installed wall belongs to the separate hub hardware issue created by #31's decomposition. Source tests do not establish visible light output.

## Required source prerequisites

- [Hub #31](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/31): general-control definition, accepted 2026-09-22.
- [#28](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/28): protected controller API, closed.

Coordinate shared-file changes under `bridge/` with the owner of the concurrent device-aware contracts work in #41. That work is not a required input here.

## Verification

Use fake device transports, disposable state and the shared contract fixtures. Cover accepted and rejected scene commands per mode, brightness override persistence and reapplication, uncertain transport holds, replay of identical requests and snapshot separation. Real client, installed runtime and visible-light evidence stay in the hardware issue.

## Work assessment

Planning assessment, 2026-09-22, against codex-nanoleaf `main` and the accepted Hub #31 decisions.

- **Complexity: medium.** Worker queue, mode policy and scene discovery interact, but the queue and guards already exist.
- **Uncertainty: low.** The behavior is accepted; the remaining brightness policy text is a bounded refinement owned here.
- **Impact: medium.** Incorrect writes affect the physical wall; the single-writer, hold and replay rules bound recovery.

**Readiness:** ready for issue-linked specification and implementation. **Review:** independent Standards and Specification reviews plus concurrency review of the mode/override interaction. **Reassessment triggers:** changed scope, a scene discovery limitation found during implementation, or blocking review findings.

## Planning and delivery

Follow AGENTS.md and docs/sdlc.md. Before behavior changes, create the exact issue-linked OpenSpec change and proportionate executable checks. Use isolated work, independent review, guarded merge and merged-revision CI. Keep credentials, private paths, agent content and runtime state out of Git. This issue does not authorize installation, device operations or settings changes.

Expected: a genuinely pending approval remains red. Once reliable evidence says that approval was resolved, the corresponding Line leaves red. If the source cannot establish the current state, the product should expose that uncertainty and provide an evidence-based recovery path; it must not silently treat an old approval as confirmed current or clear a real pending approval merely because time passed.

## Reproduction and evidence (2026-09-23 UTC)

Read-only inspection of `~/.local/share/codex-nanoleaf/status.sqlite` using SQLite `mode=ro`, `PRAGMA query_only=ON`, and a read transaction found:

- Shared input selected; collector `running`; feed received about 0.5 seconds before inspection; snapshot revision 708, loss count 0.
- Five `blocked` session records, two with assigned Lines. The assigned records were in slots **4 and 13** and both appeared in `shared_stale`.
- In the corresponding feed records, both were Codex Desktop sessions with `freshness=uncertain`, `activity=unknown`, `read=unknown`, and an `approval` attention marker. Both carried unavailable evidence for ordering, attention, turn, and activity (ambiguous or missing). Their observation ages were roughly 2.8 hours. The local `waits` table had zero rows; shared-session attention is the relevant input here.
- A focused read-only assertion for assigned, blocked, stale records returned `[(4,), (13,)]` twice, three seconds apart. The feed revision was 703 during that repeat check and later advanced to 708, while the two assigned records remained blocked and stale.

Reproduction command for the local projection (no light request or state write):

```bash
python3 -c 'import sqlite3; d=sqlite3.connect("file:/home/jimmie/.local/share/codex-nanoleaf/status.sqlite?mode=ro",uri=True); d.execute("PRAGMA query_only=ON"); d.execute("BEGIN"); x=d.execute("SELECT slot FROM slots JOIN sessions ON slots.session=sessions.id JOIN shared_stale ON slots.session=shared_stale.session WHERE sessions.status=\"blocked\" ORDER BY slot").fetchall(); print(x); assert x==[(4,),(13,)]'
# Observed: [(4,), (13,)]
```

The exact slot numbers and assertion reflect this installation; a regression fixture should assert the behavior, not those numbers. No session IDs, task titles, tokens, credentials, or raw feed payload are included here. The user's visual report establishes that two Lines appeared red; database inspection establishes their projected statuses, not a separate physical controller readback.

The current source maps approval attention to `blocked` ([`semantic_status`](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/cbb948516eb161d551d817c7ee2870b2b74dc9cb/bridge/shared_input.py#L333-L340)) and retains the old turn/status when a session is stale ([`_project`](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/cbb948516eb161d551d817c7ee2870b2b74dc9cb/bridge/shared_input.py#L355-L366)). The installed runtime uses the same relevant rule. This explains the persistent local red projection. It does **not** prove whether the original approvals are still open or identify which upstream observation became ambiguous.

## Scope

Trace the approval lifecycle across the shared state owner/collector and Nanoleaf projection. Determine why these Codex Desktop records retain ambiguous approval attention, and repair the responsible boundary so resolved approvals stop occupying red Lines while genuine approvals remain visible. Preserve the shared owner as the status authority, the single light writer, task allocations and preferences, and the established stale-data safeguards. If the defect is upstream, link and coordinate an owner-repository issue rather than reinterpreting provider events in the Nanoleaf consumer.

This issue is **source-only**. It does not authorize changing the installed runtime, resetting task state, acknowledging notices, or operating the physical lights.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A focused regression scenario reproduces uncertain/stale approval evidence retaining a red assignment after the actual approval has resolved, and distinguishes it from a genuinely pending approval.
- [x] The responsible source or projection is corrected so fresh resolution evidence clears the red status; an unresolved approval stays red. Reconnection, missing events, and uncertainty do not silently claim a resolution.
- [x] Consumer health or diagnostics make a retained uncertain status distinguishable from a confirmed current block, without exposing private session metadata or credentials.
- [x] Existing allocation, pulse/alert priority, shared-source selection, and single-writer behavior remain intact.
- [x] The fix is verified with isolated state and fake transport; any later installation and visible-light acceptance are recorded separately.

## Verification approach

Use a minimal shared snapshot/event sequence with an approval, ambiguous or missing follow-up evidence, and a reliable resolution event. Check the shared owner's semantic state, the Nanoleaf projected status and freshness, and the fake-rendered Line color at each step. Run the repository's Python checks after Python changes. If the map/API changes, run browser checks too. Do not use live credentials or reset the installed database as a test fixture.

title: Investigate and resolve retained shared unread indicators

The map server includes every session in working, question, blocked or unread status. The shared consumer derives unread from owner read and notice evidence. Trace that evidence before changing retention or presentation.

## Scope

Investigate representative unread sessions from source observation through shared owner, Nanoleaf projection and map count using sanitized aggregate evidence. Classify legitimate unread state, unavailable read evidence, delayed or missed transitions, and projection defects. Repair a confirmed defect in its owning repository, or create and link the exact upstream issue if this repository cannot own the fix. Document the supported per-notice recovery path when state is legitimately retained without read evidence.

Do not clear unread by age, truncate the API count, write Codex's private state, bulk-acknowledge notices, or reset the installed database. The approval-specific recovery delivered in [Nanoleaf #72](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/72) and [Hub #185](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/185) is related but does not establish the cause of this unread count.

- [ ] Focused fixtures cover a genuinely unread notice, qualified read evidence, explicit acknowledgment, a new turn under the configured consumer policy, uncertain or unavailable evidence, and restart/reconnect. Counts and Line allocation follow the documented state in each case.
- [ ] Any confirmed lifecycle defect is fixed at the owning boundary and verified without dropping genuine notices. If the observed growth is expected under the available evidence, record that finding and a specific supported cleanup action or separately scoped follow-up rather than claiming a code fix.

No live task acknowledgment or installation is authorized by this issue.

title: Show Codex titles and projects for shared tasks, with distinct fallback names
body:
## Problem

In shared mode, the wall names every task `Task shared-<one hex digit>` and shows no project. A read-only snapshot of the installation on 2026-09-23 had 119 shared sessions. None had a hub `label` or `projectId`, and all 72 visible tasks used the fallback name.

There are two causes:

- **The Codex metadata reader is off in shared mode.** `bridge/wall_server.py` skips the reader when shared input is selected, so Codex titles and projects never reach shared tasks. The hub feed carries only user-chosen labels and project IDs, and nothing sets them today.
- **The fallback name is too short to tell tasks apart.** It is `'Task ' + sid[:8]`. Shared keys start with `shared-`, which leaves one hex digit. Legacy keys are Codex UUIDv7 thread IDs, whose first 8 characters encode a timestamp, so tasks started close together collide too. On 2026-09-24, 32 installed sessions had only 29 distinct prefixes.

After the [#89](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/89) rollback on 2026-09-24, legacy mode shows titles and projects again because the reader is on. This issue brings the same data to shared mode.

## Outcome

Shared Codex tasks show the same titles and projects as legacy mode. Tasks without a title, such as Claude Code tasks or Codex tasks missing from the index, get a distinct, readable fallback name.

## Scope

This is a personal installation: Codex, the hub and the wall run on one host. That keeps the change small.

- **Look up Codex sessions locally.** In shared mode, keep the existing metadata reader running. For sessions whose `identity.provider` is `codex`, look up `identity.sessionId` in the configured Codex files. Apply the same title and project rules as legacy mode.
- **Do the lookup in the shared projection.** Put it in `shared_input._project`, not in the map server. The project drives Line allocation, and `_project` rewrites `task_info` on every poll.
- **Enrich only sessions in the current feed.** A lookup never creates, restores or renews a task. Retirement under [Hub #195](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/195) stays authoritative.
- **Use one precedence order.** A manual project override wins. Next comes a hub label or `projectId`, then Codex metadata. Without any of these, the task gets the fallback name and no project.
- **Build the fallback from the end of the ID.** Use the provider plus the last 8 hex characters of `identity.sessionId`, for example `Codex 5b1e07c2` or `Claude 4227761b`. Use the end because the start of a UUIDv7 is a timestamp. Legacy mode uses the same rule.
- **Document it briefly.** Add a short paragraph on precedence and the fallback name to `bridge/README.md`.

What stays the same:

- The map reads Codex files and never writes them.
- Nothing new is uploaded to the hub feed.
- The hub and its contracts do not change.

Out of scope:

- **Claude Code titles and projects from local Claude Code data.** Tracked in [#100](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/100). Until then, these tasks use the fallback name or a label set in the hub dashboard.
- **Host and source identity checks beyond the provider.** Codex thread IDs are UUIDs, so provider plus session ID is enough on one machine.
- **A provenance document, source-qualification rules and an upstream owner issue.**

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] In shared mode, a Codex session whose thread ID appears in the configured Codex files shows that title and project. Line allocation uses that project.
- [x] A Claude Code session with the same raw session ID as a Codex thread does not receive the Codex title or project.
- [x] A hub label or `projectId` wins over Codex metadata. A manual project override wins over both and survives restarts and legacy/shared switching.
- [x] Tasks without a title show the provider plus the last 8 hex characters of their session ID. Two Codex tasks started seconds apart have distinct names. No `Task shared-*` names remain.
- [x] A session that has left the feed is not recreated or renewed by the lookup.
- [x] Legacy mode behaves as before, apart from the new fallback name.
- [x] `bridge/README.md` documents the precedence order and the fallback name.

## Dependencies

- **Builds on the shared consumer.** That consumer came from [#29](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/29).
- **No hub changes are needed.**
- **Deliver this before [#89](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/89).** That issue removes the legacy hooks, and delivering this first keeps titles and projects through that cutover.

## Verification and delivery

- **Update the spec.** This needs an OpenSpec delta to `shared-session-consumer`, whose "Multiple identities" scenario currently allows only explicit bindings to connect sessions to local presentation data.
- **Test with synthetic sessions.** Cover these cases:
  - a Codex session present in the title index and project assignments
  - a Codex session missing from both
  - a Claude Code session that shares a raw session ID with a Codex thread
  - a hub label
  - a manual override
  - two Codex UUIDv7 IDs a few seconds apart
  - switching between legacy and shared mode
- **Run the checks.** Run `python3 scripts/check.py`, `npm run test:browser`, and the OpenSpec workflow checks.
- **Get human approval.** The fallback name is a UI change.
- **Deliver as source only.** Ship through one reviewed PR. Installation is separate.

title: Queue the completion comet when a subagent delays a parent's unread
body:
## Problem

After [#74](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/74) ([PR #80](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/pull/80)), subagent sessions count as part of their parent task. A parent's completion can then skip its celebration comet. This happens when the parent's turn ends while the owner still counts a subagent active.

When the parent's turn-ended notice first appears, the task still shows working because of that subagent, so no comet is queued. When the subagent later finishes or goes silent, the task becomes unread. By then the notice was already present in the prior snapshot, and the consumer queues comets only for notices that are new relative to the prior snapshot. The unread color and its outward wave still show; only the one-time comet is lost. This was found in PR #80's round-5 Standards review, finding S12.

## Desired outcome

A top-level completion notice queues one completion comet the first time its task becomes visibly unread, even when a subagent delayed that transition. A notice that was already celebrated is never celebrated again. That includes a task that returns to unread after a subagent's later work.

## Scope and acceptance criteria

- [ ] The parent's notice arrives while a subagent is counted active. The subagent then finishes or goes silent, and exactly one comet is queued in Work.
- [ ] A notice that was already celebrated while its task was unread is not celebrated again when a later subagent run ends.
- [ ] Interruption, resync, stale evidence and Free/Quiet keep their existing comet rules. Started comet reservations are unaffected.
- [ ] Any retained celebration state is private and survives restart without replaying old comets. Legacy mode is unchanged.

## Verification

Add focused `tests/test_shared_input.py` cases using the fake clock and isolated state, and run `python3 scripts/check.py`. If behavior changes, update the `shared-session-consumer` spec through an OpenSpec change.

## Dependencies

Requires #74 / PR #80 to be merged. This is source-only work; it needs no installation or device checks.

title: Remove the legacy Codex hooks after the shared-input cutover
body:
## Outcome

With shared input selected, Codex no longer runs the legacy `bridge.py hook` on every event. One command removes those hooks, and one command restores them for a rollback to legacy input.

## Why

The legacy hook is still registered for seven events in both Codex homes, including PreToolUse and PostToolUse, so it runs twice per tool call. In shared mode, `handle_event` reads `config.json`, opens `status.sqlite`, takes its write lock twice and returns without doing anything else. Each run costs about 50 ms of Python startup and imports. Codex waits for these hooks. If one arrives while the worker holds the write lock during a device write, it can wait up to 2.5 s before failing open.

The hub's shared hook covers the events that shared mode uses, and it doesn't register PreToolUse or PostToolUse. Removing the legacy hooks loses only the rollback path. `shared-select legacy` depends on legacy hook events to clear restored steady colors and to create new tasks.

There is no supported way to remove only these hooks. `setup --uninstall` removes them but also switches every device to Free. Running a fresh `setup` to add them back clears task records.

## Scope

- [x] `hooks remove` deletes only the entries tagged `nanoleaf-codex-status-v1` from a Codex home's `hooks.json`. Every other entry, including the hub's shared hook, stays byte for byte. It keeps a private backup outside Git and changes no mode, task or device state.
- [x] `hooks register` adds them back without running `setup`.
- [x] Both commands take the Codex home explicitly, so the WSL home (Codex CLI) and the Windows home (Codex Desktop) can each be handled.
- [x] `hooks remove` refuses while legacy input is selected. `shared-select legacy` refuses when the legacy hooks are missing from `$CODEX_HOME`, and its message names `hooks register`.
- [x] `docs/shared-input.md` and `docs/linux-install.md` describe the cutover and the rollback order: register the hooks, then run `shared-select legacy`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Tests with temporary Codex homes cover:
  - removal of only the tagged entries
  - repeated remove and register
  - hub and unrelated entries preserved
  - the backup
  - both refusals
  - a malformed `hooks.json` left untouched
- [x] `python3 scripts/check.py` passes.
- [x] Live, when the owner explicitly requests the installed change: remove the legacy hooks from both Codex homes and confirm the wall still follows a Codex prompt through shared input. One comment records it.

## Not included

Removing or changing the hub's shared hook and its setup tooling, the legacy Windows installation, and Claude Code hooks.

## Readiness

Complexity small. Uncertainty low. No blockers. The hub's AGENTS.md keeps the legacy hooks until an authorized, verified cutover; the live step is that cutover. Delivery follows docs/sdlc.md.

title: Wake the worker from the hub's change stream instead of polling each second
body:
## Outcome

The wall reacts to a new hub revision as soon as the hub announces it, instead of on the worker's next 1-second poll.

## Current behavior

In shared mode, `Poller.tick` fetches `GET /api/monitor/v1/sessions` at the start of each worker pass, at most once a second. Between passes the worker sleeps in 0.25 s steps and wakes early only for local changes (`event_revision` or a preview). A hub revision reaches `PUT /effects` about 0 to 1.3 s later, plus device round trips.

The hub also serves `GET /api/monitor/v1/changes`, a Server-Sent Events stream that announces a new revision without carrying session data. Nanoleaf doesn't use it. The hub currently checks for changes on a 1-second timer, so listening won't help until [agent-device-hub#222](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/222) makes it push on commit.

## Scope

- [ ] A listener thread in the shared-input worker keeps `/changes` open with the existing read token and endpoint checks (numeric loopback only, owner-only token file). It sends `Last-Event-ID` when it reconnects.
- [ ] A `state` or `resync` event wakes the worker, which fetches `/sessions` at once through the existing poller. The snapshot stays the only source of session state.
- [ ] The worker's sleep ends on that signal as well as on local changes.
- [ ] Polling stays as the fallback. While the stream is healthy the poll can slow down, for example to 5 s. When the stream is down it returns to 1 s. Choose the values during delivery.
- [ ] The listener is bounded: a connect deadline, a reconnect when heartbeats stop for a few seconds, backoff and no unbounded buffering. A stream failure alone never marks sessions stale; staleness still comes only from failed snapshot fetches.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tests with a fake hub stream cover:
  - an event that triggers an immediate fetch
  - `resync`
  - reconnecting with `Last-Event-ID`
  - a stream that goes silent
  - the stream being down while polling still works
- [ ] An event with no snapshot change sends nothing to the panels.
- [ ] `python3 scripts/check.py` passes, and an OpenSpec change updates the `shared-session-consumer` spec.
- [ ] Live, when the owner explicitly requests the installed update and hub #222 is installed: submit a Codex prompt and confirm the wall reacts. One comment records it.

## Dependencies

Blocked by [agent-device-hub#222](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/222).

## Not included

Tidbyt, the hub dashboard and any change to the session snapshot format.

## Readiness

Complexity small to medium. Uncertainty low. Backlog until hub #222 merges. Delivery follows docs/sdlc.md.

title: Let Codex play saved Nanoleaf scenes through the local MCP server
body:
## Outcome

You can ask Codex to play a scene you saved in the Nanoleaf app, for example "switch the wall to Free and play Aurora", through the local MCP server.

## Current behavior

The controller already supports `scene.activate` for discovered scenes, in Free mode only (#64). The local MCP server exposes only `nanoleaf_status` and `nanoleaf_mode_set`, and the `local-mcp-bindings` spec forbids scene tools. Scene IDs are opaque. The names you chose in the Nanoleaf app travel in the `nanoleaf.integration/1.0` snapshot. Codex isn't configured to use the MCP server yet.

## Scope

- [ ] A read tool lists the advertised scenes with their IDs and names.
- [ ] A control tool, `nanoleaf_scene_activate`, sends one `scene.activate` through the controller. Like `nanoleaf_mode_set`, it passes the caller's request ID and expected revisions through unchanged.
- [ ] Following hub ADR 0005, activation stays a separate command. The tool doesn't switch to Free itself. In Work or Quiet it returns the controller's rejection with a message to switch to Free first.
- [ ] An unknown scene ID is rejected before dispatch. The tools appear only for credentials with the matching read or control scope.
- [ ] An OpenSpec change updates the `local-mcp-bindings` spec, and `docs/local-mcp.md` describes the tools.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Fake-controller tests cover:
  - listing
  - activation in Free
  - rejection in Work and Quiet
  - an unknown scene
  - scope filtering
  - receipts preserved without claiming visible output
- [ ] `python3 scripts/check.py` and `npm run test:mcp` pass.
- [ ] Live, when the owner explicitly requests the Codex configuration change: register the server with `codex mcp add nanoleaf --url http://127.0.0.1:41230/mcp --bearer-token-env-var NANOLEAF_MCP_TOKEN`, then ask Codex to switch to Free and play a named scene. One comment records it.

## Not included

Power and brightness tools, custom animations, the hub's MCP route, the NL22 Panels, and ChatGPT or other remote clients.

## Readiness

Complexity small. Uncertainty low. No blockers. Delivery follows docs/sdlc.md.

title: Play custom animations on the Lines when Codex asks for them
body:
## Outcome

You can describe an animation to Codex, such as "a slow blue-green ocean wave". Codex switches the wall to Free and plays it on the Lines through the local MCP server.

## Background

A custom Nanoleaf animation is a `display` effect: frames for each panel, uploaded once with `PUT /effects` and then looped by the device. The worker already builds and uploads this kind of effect for status (`effect_payload` in `bridge/bridge.py`). A requested animation reuses the same path and the same single writer, with no per-frame streaming.

Nothing accepts animation input today. Controller v1 has no animation command. The hub architecture requires typed-extension work for arbitrary color or timeline input and rules out raw protocol commands.

## Decision

The owner chose Free-mode content on September 23, 2026. When you ask for an animation in conversation, the agent switches the wall to Free with `nanoleaf_mode_set`, then plays the animation. It stays until the next mode command, animation or scene. This fits hub [ADR 0005](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/blob/main/docs/decisions/0005-general-device-controls.md) as written: switching to Free is its own command, and nothing restores automatically.

Animations that play over Work status to get your attention are wanted too, but as scheduled or routine behavior, not on request. They are out of scope here (see Not included).

## Scope

- [ ] A typed `animation.play` command in the Nanoleaf extension, not a controller v1 change. Parameters: a pattern from a fixed set (for example wave, pulse, breathe, sparkle and gradient), 1 to 8 `#rrggbb` colors, speed, direction for spatial patterns, and whether it loops or plays once. The controller validates everything before queueing.
- [ ] The worker separates the frame encoder from the status color logic, and renders each pattern with the Lines geometry it already uses for waves and comets.
- [ ] Commands use the existing queue and receipts: sent, failed or uncertain, with physical outcome unknown. Like `scene.activate`, the command is accepted only in Free. In Work or Quiet the controller rejects it before any write, and the MCP tool's message says to switch to Free first.
- [ ] The local MCP server gets a read tool that lists patterns and limits, and a control tool, `nanoleaf_animation_play`.
- [ ] Qualify the firmware's limits on effect size and frame count, and keep requests within the controller's 64 KiB limit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tests cover validation bounds, encoder output for each pattern on fixture layouts, acceptance in Free and rejection in Work and Quiet, receipts and the MCP tools.
- [ ] `python3 scripts/check.py` and `npm run test:mcp` pass. OpenSpec changes update the affected controller, worker and MCP specs.
- [ ] Live, when the owner explicitly requests it: ask Codex for two different animations, and confirm it switches the wall to Free before each one plays. One comment records it.

## Related

- #91 lets Codex play saved scenes and sets up the same MCP connection.
- #19 and #20 (status animation presets) could reuse the new encoder.
- #15 (authoritative rendering state).
- [agent-device-hub#41](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/41) needs real-time streaming for music visualizers. This issue doesn't.

## Not included

Per-panel keyframes, the NL22 Panels, audio-reactive or streamed effects, and the hub's MCP route. Also attention animations over Work status: they belong with scheduled or routine behavior under [agent-device-hub#45](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/45), and playing over status will need its own ADR 0005 decision. They can reuse this issue's encoder. Also ChatGPT and other remote clients: ChatGPT connects to MCP servers only over remote HTTPS, which depends on the remote access that hub ADR 0004 defers.

## Readiness

Complexity medium. Uncertainty low; the firmware limits are the main unknown. No blockers. Delivery follows docs/sdlc.md.

title: Show Claude Code titles and projects for shared tasks
body:
## Problem

After [#75](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/75), shared Codex tasks get titles and projects from Codex's local files. Claude Code tasks still show only the fallback name, such as `Claude 4227761b`, and no project, unless someone sets a label in the hub dashboard. The hub feed does not carry Claude Code titles or working folders, by design.

## Evidence

A read-only check on 2026-09-24 found:

- **The session ID matches the transcript name.** The hub uses the Claude Code hook's `session_id` as `identity.sessionId` (`packages/agent-state/src/providers.ts` in agent-device-hub). Claude Code stores each session at `~/.claude/projects/<encoded folder>/<session_id>.jsonl`. All 1,606 `custom-title` entries in the 40 most recent WSL transcripts carried the same `sessionId` as their file name.
- **Most sessions have a title.** 33 of those 40 transcripts contain a `custom-title` entry, whose `customTitle` field holds the title. The entry repeats, so the last one is current.
- **Sessions record their folder.** `user` entries carry `cwd`. 27 of the 40 transcripts used one `cwd`. The rest changed folder during the session, for example into a worktree.
- **Codex project roots already match WSL paths.** 30 of 31 Codex project roots are `\\wsl.localhost\...` paths. The existing `normalize` in `bridge/project_map.py` converts these to Linux paths, so the legacy root-prefix rule can match a Claude Code `cwd` to a Codex project.
- **There are two Claude Code homes.** WSL has `~/.claude`, and Windows has `%USERPROFILE%\.claude`. It is not yet known which one feeds the hub.

## Outcome

Shared Claude Code tasks show their Claude Code title. When a task's working folder is inside a Codex project root, the task also shows that project.

## Scope

- **Look up Claude Code sessions locally.** For sessions whose `identity.provider` is `claude`, read the transcript named `identity.sessionId` in the configured Claude Code home. Do this in `shared_input._project`, alongside the #75 lookup.
- **Title:** use the latest `customTitle` in the transcript.
- **Project:** match the session's `cwd` against Codex project roots with the existing `normalize` and root-prefix rule. A folder outside every root gets no project.
- **Precedence:** keep the #75 order. A manual override wins, then a hub label or `projectId`, then local metadata, then the fallback name.
- **Read incrementally.** Transcripts are large and grow while a session runs. Cache per file by size and modification time, and read only new bytes or the tail. Never parse a whole transcript on every poll.
- **Tolerate format changes.** The transcript format is internal to Claude Code and undocumented. A missing file, unreadable line or unknown shape leaves the fallback name and no project, and the projection still succeeds.
- **Read only what is needed.** Take `custom-title` and `cwd` only. Never read prompt or message content into the wall's state, logs or browser responses.

What stays the same:

- The map never writes Claude Code files.
- Nothing new is uploaded to the hub feed.

## Decisions to settle before ready

- **Which Claude Code home to read:** WSL, Windows, or both. Also the configuration keys that name them.
- **Which `cwd` to use when a session changes folder:** the first, the latest, or the most frequent.
- **What to show when there is no `custom-title`:** keep the fallback name, or derive a title such as the folder name.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A shared Claude Code session whose transcript has a `custom-title` shows the latest title.
- [ ] A Claude Code session whose `cwd` is inside a Codex project root shows that project, and Line allocation uses it. Other sessions have no project.
- [ ] A Codex session with the same raw session ID as a Claude Code transcript does not receive the Claude Code title or project.
- [ ] Hub labels, hub `projectId` values and manual overrides keep the #75 precedence.
- [ ] A missing, unreadable or unrecognized transcript leaves the fallback name and no project, and the projection still succeeds.
- [ ] Polling cost stays bounded as transcripts grow.
- [ ] No prompt or message content appears in the wall's state, logs or browser responses.
- [ ] `bridge/README.md` documents the Claude Code source and its limits.

## Dependencies

- [#75](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/75): the shared-mode lookup, precedence order and fallback name.
- The decisions listed above.

## Verification and delivery

- **Update the spec.** Extend the #75 OpenSpec delta to Claude Code.
- **Test with synthetic transcripts.** Cover these cases:
  - with and without a `custom-title`
  - several `custom-title` entries
  - a folder change during the session
  - a `cwd` inside and outside a Codex project root
  - a large file that grows between polls
  - a malformed line
  - a Codex session that shares the raw session ID
- **Run the checks.** Run `python3 scripts/check.py`, `npm run test:browser`, and the OpenSpec workflow checks.
- **Deliver as source only.** Ship through one reviewed PR. Installation is separate.

title: Open a wall task's thread in Codex Desktop
body:
## Problem

The wall map shows each task's title, project and status, but gives no way to get from a task to its conversation. To continue a task, the user has to find the thread in Codex Desktop by name.

## Evidence

A read-only check on 2026-09-24 found:

- **Codex Desktop opens thread links.** The installed app (`OpenAI.Codex_26.917.9434.0`, MSIX) registers the `codex://` scheme on Windows. Its deep-link parser maps `codex://threads/<threadId>` to a local conversation and accepts an optional `hostId`. Codex's own "Copy deep link" action produces the same form. The format is internal and undocumented, so a later Codex release could change it.
- **Legacy task IDs are Desktop thread UUIDs.** The unread reader compares Desktop thread IDs directly against `sessions.id` (`bridge/bridge.py:281-283`), and `/api/state` already sends that ID to the browser.
- **Shared task IDs are hashes.** The key is `'shared-' + sha256(identity)` (`bridge/shared_input.py:31`, `:59-60`). The raw `identity.provider`, `client` and `sessionId` survive only in the stored envelope (`bridge/shared_input.py:207`, `:479`). Subagents fold into their top-level ancestor (`bridge/shared_input.py:362-379`).
- **Desktop can open only its own threads.** Codex Desktop and the WSL CLI keep separate homes. The Desktop index (`%USERPROFILE%\.codex\session_index.jsonl`) had 295 threads and the WSL index 33, with none in common.
- **The link is clicked on the same machine.** The map is opened in the Windows browser at `http://127.0.0.1:8765`, next to Codex Desktop. The map's CSP (`bridge/wall_server.py:147-152`) sets no navigation restriction, so a top-level link to `codex://` should not be blocked. The browser asks "Open Codex?" the first time and offers "Always allow".

## Desired outcome

The inspector's task detail card shows an "Open in Codex" link for Codex Desktop tasks. Clicking it opens that thread in Codex Desktop.

## Scope

- **Expose the link from the server.** `/api/state` adds `codexUrl` to a task only when it is a Desktop thread:
  - Legacy: the task ID is a UUID present in the configured Desktop title index.
  - Shared: the presented root session has `identity.provider` `codex`, `identity.client` `desktop` and a UUID `sessionId`.
- **Build the URL safely.** The server validates the UUID and builds `codex://threads/<uuid>`. The browser never builds the URL from free text.
- **Render a real link.** Put a labelled, keyboard-reachable `<a href>` without `target` in the task detail card built by `inspect()` (`bridge/wall.html:856-886`). Add `codexUrl` to the card's fingerprint (`bridge/wall.html:868`) so the card refreshes when the link appears or changes.
- **Show nothing for other tasks.** Codex CLI, Claude Code, non-UUID and unknown tasks get no link.
- **Correct the footer.** It says "Opening a task here does not mark it read" (`bridge/wall.html:398`). Selecting a task in the map still does not mark it read. Opening it in Codex lets Codex mark it read, and the bridge follows through the existing unread reader.
- **Document it.** Describe the link, which tasks get it and the read behavior in `bridge/README.md`.

What stays the same:

- Clicking the link sends no request to the map server. The map writes no Codex data and marks nothing read.
- The controller and integration APIs do not gain the URL.
- The hub and its contracts do not change.

Out of scope:

- **Links in task rows.** Keeps the reduced controls planned in #78.
- **Claude Code sessions.** No deep link was investigated. Track separately if wanted.
- **Codex CLI threads and remote `hostId` hosts.**
- **Lively and the inspection-only display mode** (#12, #14).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A legacy task whose thread is in the Desktop index shows "Open in Codex" with href `codex://threads/<id>`. Clicking it in the Windows browser opens that thread in Codex Desktop.
- [ ] A shared Codex Desktop task shows the link for its root session. A subagent task folded into its parent links to the parent's thread.
- [ ] Codex CLI tasks, Claude Code tasks and tasks with a non-UUID or unknown ID show no link.
- [ ] Clicking the link issues no request to the map server, and no write, unread acknowledgment, Locate or device request.
- [ ] Unread state clears only through the existing unread reader after Codex marks the thread read.
- [ ] The link is keyboard reachable, has an accessible label, and fits narrow layouts without horizontal overflow.
- [ ] `bridge/README.md` documents the link, its eligibility rule and the read behavior.

## Verification approach

- **Update the spec.** Add an OpenSpec delta to `wall-task-inspector`, and to `shared-session-consumer` for exposing a link derived from the shared identity.
- **Python tests** for `codexUrl`: a legacy thread in the index, a legacy thread missing from it, a shared Desktop session, a shared CLI session, a Claude Code session, a folded subagent and a malformed ID.
- **Browser test** (`npm run test:browser`): the link's href and label, keyboard access, a narrow viewport, the updated footer, and no non-GET request when the link is activated.
- **Run the checks.** `python3 scripts/check.py`, `npm run test:browser` and the OpenSpec workflow checks.
- **Manual Windows check.** Open one real Desktop thread from the map in the Windows browser. Report it separately from installation and physical-light checks, which this issue does not need.
- **Get human approval.** This is a UI change.

## Dependencies

- **Land after #75.** It changes how shared sessions' `identity` reaches the projection, which this issue also reads.
- **Land after #105.** It changes inspector selection, in the same code as the detail card.
- **Shared assumption with #75:** for Codex Desktop sessions, the hub's `identity.sessionId` is the Desktop thread UUID.

## Delivery target

Source-only.

title: Switch Nanoleaf between Work and Free based on monitored session presence
body:
## Desired outcome

For an explicitly enabled Nanoleaf device, enter native Work mode while the selected shared owner has monitored sessions, and enter native Free mode when the last session ends or expires.

User-approved behavior, September 24, 2026:

- Waiting, completed and read-but-still-tracked sessions keep Work enabled between prompts.
- Free uses the existing native scene/app handoff.
- A manual Work/Quiet/Free selection pauses automation until explicit re-enable, including across restart.
- Automation is Nanoleaf-only and disabled by default.

This changes the selected mode. Existing Work-mode idle scene restoration alone does not provide that mode switch.

## Bounded implementation

Use the existing Nanoleaf worker, feed reads and guarded native mode operation. No new daemon, scheduler, rules engine, provider hook, dashboard or restoration-history service.

### One persistent setting

Use one automation-enabled boolean per participating registered device:

- Explicit enable sets it to true and reconciles current session presence.
- Explicit disable sets it to false without an extra mode command.
- A user mode command sets it to false, including selection of the already-current mode. Automatic commands do not disable themselves.
- Persist the flag. A separate paused state, resume-cycle counter, reason history or saved pre-Work mode is unnecessary.
- Provide local enable, disable and status controls. Do not discover or enroll devices automatically.

Apply manual precedence through the existing shared mode operation used by the CLI, wall map, tray and controller API. Preserve its guards so pending automatic decisions cannot override a newer manual selection.

### One presence rule

When enabled and the feed is valid with a running owner:

| Owner snapshot | Desired native mode |
| --- | --- |
| One or more session records | Work |
| No session records | Free |
| Feed missing, invalid, disconnected or owner not running | Hold current mode |

Count all session records in the selected feed, including children and all supported provider/client paths. Do not count only `activity: active`, visible rows or allocated Lines. The shared owner decides retirement; Nanoleaf adds no provider interpretation.

Reconcile on presence changes, explicit enable, startup and recovery using the current snapshot. Skip a command when the desired mode is already selected. Additional starts/ends while presence remains nonzero cause no mode write. Repeated polls and duplicate snapshots do not repeatedly command devices; do not replay missed transitions. A retire/resume interval unseen between reads need not cause a pointless Free/Work cycle.

Retain existing bounded controller failure handling and receipts. Yield on observed external control or conflicts rather than repeatedly taking over; do not add vendor-app detection. Keep one writer per device and independent failures. Preserve native power-off behavior, Work/Free scene and brightness policies, reservations and task/effect state. Add no power/brightness commands, selected-scene override or old-effect replay.

This explicitly enabled automation is a narrow exception to manual-only mode selection. Update the owning mode/shared-input specification and guide during implementation; leave other device families and hub preset policy unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Disabled automation sends no mode commands. Enable/disable/status reflect the persisted flag.
- [ ] First session presence requests Work once; the last record's removal requests Free once. Multiple sessions and child records keep presence nonzero.
- [ ] Ordinary completion, waiting, read/acknowledgment changes, five-minute freshness uncertainty and turns exceeding 30 minutes do not cause Free. Owner retirement/expiry does.
- [ ] Every existing explicit mode-command entry point disables automation, even for the current mode. The flag survives restart/reconnect; only explicit re-enable resumes automation.
- [ ] Invalid/unavailable feeds hold the current mode. Startup, recovery and enable reconcile a current valid snapshot without historical replay.
- [ ] Duplicate snapshots, quick end/resume, repeated polls and concurrent manual selection cause no redundant mode writes or manual override reversal.
- [ ] Focused fake-device checks preserve native Free handoff, power-off, scenes/brightness, reservations and no-old-effect-replay behavior. Failures and uncertain outcomes remain bounded and do not affect other devices.

## Verification approach

Extend existing isolated-state, fake-clock, shared-feed and fake-device tests for the scenarios above. Reuse existing mode/queue coverage rather than duplicate controller suites. Add issue-linked OpenSpec artifacts and affected guide/development updates, and run applicable repository checks. There is no new UI scope.

Installation and visible-light verification remain separate, requiring a named owner, explicit target and authorized sequence. Observe first-session Work, last-session Free, a long turn, manual disable and restart/reconnect behavior. Source or transport success is not physical acceptance.

## Dependencies and delivery target

- **Blocked by [Hub #218](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/218)** for prompt Codex Desktop retirement. Other providers retain the owner's existing retention policy. Next action: deliver that removal contract, then validate this consumer against it.
- Existing prerequisites are complete: [shared sessions #29](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/29), [per-device workers #42](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/42) and [native controls #64](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/64).
- [Hub #67](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/67) owns explicit multi-device presets; [Hub #45](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/agent-device-hub/issues/45) owns broader automation. Neither is a prerequisite.

Source-only; backlog/blocked on Hub #218. Scope simplified with the user on September 24, 2026 without changing the accepted behavior. This tracker revision authorizes no implementation, installation, personal settings change or physical device operation.

title: Keep following the hub feed when it contains an undeclared source
body:
## Problem

Nanoleaf rejects the whole hub snapshot when any session comes from a source that isn't in `qualifiedSources`. `check_envelope` in `bridge/shared_input.py` raises `unqualified-source`. The feed then counts as failed: tasks are marked stale, colors hold and the wall stops following every agent, not just the new one. It stays that way until someone edits the consumer configuration.

The installed configuration declares only Codex Desktop and Codex CLI. The hub has no Claude Code sessions today, but the first Claude Code hook that posts to it would stop the wall. #100 expects Claude Code tasks on the wall.

## Outcome

A session from a source Nanoleaf hasn't declared stays off the wall, and every other session keeps updating. Once you declare a Claude Code source, its sessions appear.

## Scope

- [ ] Skip sessions from undeclared sources instead of rejecting the snapshot. A skipped session gets no slot, wave, comet or acknowledgment, and takes no part in parent and subagent grouping.
- [ ] Envelope checks still reject the whole snapshot: authentication, version, owner, schema and revision.
- [ ] `shared-status` reports how many sessions were skipped and their source identities, so a missing declaration is visible.
- [ ] Declaring a source later with `shared-configure` doesn't replay old comets or waves for its existing sessions.
- [ ] Test that `qualifiedSources` accepts a Claude Code source identity. Update `docs/shared-input.md`, which says every source in the feed must be declared, and describe how to declare one.
- [ ] An OpenSpec change updates the `shared-session-consumer` spec.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tests cover:
  - one undeclared session among declared ones
  - a snapshot with only undeclared sessions, which leaves the wall idle and the connection current
  - a declared Claude Code source
  - declaring a source after its sessions already exist
  - a declared subagent whose parent is undeclared, which follows the existing missing-parent rule
- [ ] `python3 scripts/check.py` passes.

## Dependencies

Blocks #100.

## Not included

Installing Claude Code hooks for the hub, and any hub change.

## Readiness

Complexity small. Uncertainty low. No blockers. Delivery follows docs/sdlc.md.

title: Show when the Lines are on hold and how to resume them
body:
## Problem

After a device write with an uncertain result, or a controller command that stays queued for more than 30 s, the worker puts the Lines on hold (`controller_hold_revision`). It stops writing to them so it never repeats a write that may already have landed. To you, the wall just looks frozen on its last display.

Nothing says why. The controller snapshot reports the failed or uncertain `lastOutcome` but not the hold, and the wall map doesn't show it.

Any mode command clears the hold, even one that selects the mode already active. That works from the wall map, CLI, controller or MCP. Power and brightness commands through the controller clear it too.

## Outcome

When the Lines are on hold, the wall map says so, explains why and offers one action to resume.

## Scope

- [ ] The wall map shows the hold, when it started and its cause (an uncertain write or an expired command), with a Resume action that selects the current mode again.
- [ ] The message explains that the worker paused so it wouldn't repeat a write that may have landed.
- [ ] The CLI's status output reports the hold the same way.
- [ ] Resume uses the existing mode path. Nothing retries automatically.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tests cover a hold from an uncertain write, a hold from an expired command, Resume clearing it, and no hold shown after a mode, power or brightness command.
- [ ] `python3 scripts/check.py` and `npm run test:browser` pass. The PR includes a wall map screenshot in the held state.

## Not included

Showing the hold in the hub dashboard. That needs the `nanoleaf.integration` snapshot to carry it, which changes a schema the hub validates, so it is a separate change in both repositories.

## Readiness

Complexity small. Uncertainty low. No blockers. Delivery follows docs/sdlc.md.

title: Control the NL22 Panels through the controller and local MCP server
body:
## Problem

The protected controller and the local MCP server reach only the Lines (`wall`). The controller has one device identity. Under ADR 0010, only the `wall` worker runs controller and integration work, including overrides, the hold and scene discovery. The NL22 Panels can be controlled only from the CLI (`mode … --device panels`).

So the hub, the dashboard and Codex can't turn the Panels on or off, set their brightness or mode, or play their scenes. #91 and #92 cover the Lines only.

## Outcome

The Panels are a second controller device. The hub, the dashboard and Codex (through MCP) control them the same way as the Lines, and each device keeps its own single writer.

## Scope

- [ ] `/controller/v1/devices` lists both devices. The snapshot, commands, feed and integration routes accept the Panels' `deviceId`, with their own identity, revisions, request journal, overrides, hold and discovered scenes.
- [ ] The Panels worker runs the Panels' controller work and stays the only writer to the Panels. The `wall` worker never writes to them. Update ADR 0010, which assigns all controller work to `wall`.
- [ ] Power, brightness, mode and `scene.activate` work for the Panels under the same mode rules as the Lines.
- [ ] The local MCP server can bind the Panels as a second fixed target. Callers can't choose other devices.
- [ ] Record whether the Panels accept `display` version 2.0 effects, which ADR 0010 lists as unknown. #92 needs that answer before animations can extend to the Panels.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tests with fake devices cover both devices side by side:
  - a command for one device never runs on the other's worker
  - a hold on one device doesn't affect the other
  - each device keeps its own revisions and scenes
- [ ] `python3 scripts/check.py` and `npm run test:mcp` pass. OpenSpec changes update the affected controller, worker and MCP specs.
- [ ] Live, when the owner explicitly requests it: add a hub controller entry for the Panels, then change their mode and brightness from the dashboard or Codex. One comment records it.

## Related

- #91 and #92 add scenes and animations for the Lines. Both can extend to the Panels after this.
- #44 and #47 cover the wall map and a combined layout.

## Readiness

Complexity medium. Uncertainty medium: the ADR 0010 ownership change is the main design work. No blockers. Delivery follows docs/sdlc.md.

title: Change a registered Nanoleaf device's address without re-enrolling
body:
## Desired outcome

Let the operator change the address of a registered Nanoleaf device, such as the NL22 Light Panels after a new DHCP lease, without removing and re-enrolling it. The device keeps its id, reservations, mode, layout and saved scene.

This is a personal project with one operator and one Linux installation. The issue is sized for that.

## Background

`device-enroll` ([#45](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/issues/45), PR #79) refuses an existing id at a new address, so it never silently redirects an identity. The only way to change a Panels address today is `device-remove` followed by `device-enroll`, which clears the device's reservations. The [device-state specification](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/blob/main/openspec/specs/device-state/spec.md) already says a configured address change keeps a device's identity and saved state. The Linux guide documents the current workaround.

## Scope

An explicit command or option that changes one registered device's address. Before writing, it verifies the device at the new address with the stored credential, the same way enrollment does: model NL22 and a layout whose triangles match the saved geometry. The Lines device (`wall`) may be covered if that is simple; otherwise it is out of scope.

Out of scope: automatic discovery or following the device on the network, and changing a device's kind.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1: The operator can change a registered Panels device's address. Its id, reservations, mode, layout and saved scene are unchanged, and it is never registered twice.
- [ ] AC2: Before any write, the new address is checked: it must be a private IPv4 address, unused by another registered device, and answering as the same kind of device with a layout matching the saved one. A mismatch is refused with nothing changed.
- [ ] AC3: The change sends no light write. A running worker for the device picks up the new address on its next pass or retry, without a service restart.
- [ ] AC4: Credentials stay out of output and errors, as with enrollment.
- [ ] AC5: The Linux installation guide replaces the remove-and-re-enroll workaround with the new command.

## Verification approach

Isolated Linux state with fake Lines and NL22 transports. Cover a successful change, a conflicting address, a device that does not match, an unreachable address, and a worker picking up the new address. Run the Python and workflow suites.

## Dependencies

- Builds on #45 (delivered). Not needed for #46 unless the Panels' address changes during that trial.

## Delivery target

Source only. Changing the installed runtime's device address is a separate operator action.

title: Keep completion comets and waves when the worker skips owner revisions
body:
## Problem

In shared mode, the Nanoleaf worker treats any skipped owner revision as a resync (`bridge/shared_input.py`, `_project`: `snapshot['revision'] > previous['snapshot']['revision'] + 1`). A resync:

- sets `shared_wave_cutoff`, so outward waves from earlier epochs are suppressed, and any new or changed status gets an expired epoch;
- deletes every task's comets, including celebrations that are already running;
- skips the unread-comet check, because that check sits in an `elif` after the resync branch.

The worker polls the owner at most once a second, and the Hub commits a revision for every accepted hook event. Two commits between polls are therefore routine: a parent's Stop plus a SubagentStop, or events from another session. When that happens, a new completion gets neither its comet nor its wave, and any running comet stops early.

A skipped revision loses no state. Every snapshot is the owner's complete current state, so only the intermediate transitions go unobserved. A real resync is needed only for evidence of loss (`lossCount` or `admissionRejected` changing), a reconnect, or no previous envelope.

This was found during the #74 closeout ([PR #80](https://github.com/jimmie-potts/codex-nanoleaf/pull/80)). Related:
- #81, the subagent-specific case of a comet being decided by comparing against the previous snapshot;
- #90, waking on the Hub's change stream, which narrows the window but doesn't close it.

## Desired outcome

A revision gap with no loss evidence is treated as an ordinary update. A new top-level completion notice queues its comet and wave once, however many revisions the worker skipped. Running comets and existing wave epochs continue. A real loss, a reconnect or a restart keeps today's no-replay resync behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A completion arrives in a revision the worker never observes, with a later revision in the same poll. Exactly one comet is queued in Work, and the unread wave plays.
- [ ] A running comet and other tasks' wave epochs survive a revision gap.
- [ ] A `lossCount` or `admissionRejected` change, a reconnect and a first snapshot still resync without replaying old celebrations.
- [ ] A notice that was already celebrated is not celebrated again after a gap. Coordinate the "already celebrated" definition with #81.
- [ ] Stale evidence, Free/Quiet and started comet reservations keep their existing rules.
